![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14246974/assets/e006f41f3c8a0201623c88bd4f3738bea05258690c8a0adef297769341a3f490.png)

Given that $r$, $s$ and $t$ in the above diagram are parallel, find $m∠1.$
q-158686.worked_solution:
Consider $∠2$ in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14246974/assets/2bca55a68d4a0695c73f82ca82d5fae386d9b8d57b058bc1cf694bee902cff25.png)

Notice that $∠2$ and the angle whose measure is ${42}^{∘}$ are alternate exterior angles formed when the transversal $u$ cuts the parallel lines $r$ and $s.$ Hence, 

$$
m∠2={42}^{∘}.
$$

Also, notice that the angle determined by $∠1$ and $∠2$ and the angle whose measure is ${108}^{∘}$ are corresponding angles formed when the transversal $v$ cuts the parallel lines $s$ and $t.$ Hence, 

$$
m∠1+m∠2={108}^{∘}.
$$

Now, substituting $m∠2$ into the equation, we can find $m∠1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠1+m∠2 & ={108}^{∘} \\ m∠1+{42}^{∘} & ={108}^{∘} \\ m∠1 & ={66}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

q-158701.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14246974/assets/5178d7f2910b4a28116022968e6a2d5580b9284d65bb7dc973e36f4c2a2f4ccd.png)

Given that $\overset{↔}{AB}∥\overset{↔}{CF},$ what is the measure of $∠AFB?$
q-158701.worked_solution:
Notice that $∠BAF$  and $∠AFC$ are alternate interior angles formed when the transversal $\overset{↔}{AF}$ cuts the parallel lines $\overset{↔}{AB}$ and $\overset{↔}{CF}.$ Hence, 

$$
m∠AFC=m∠BAF={71}^{∘}.
$$

 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14246974/assets/bfb1ce1e2aba3efe901251ad40f84fda062e8324c4dd7a1f2888081724679842.png)

Also, notice that $∠FBE$  and $∠BFC$ are alternate interior angles formed when the transversal $\overset{↔}{BF}$ cuts the parallel lines $\overset{↔}{AB}$ and $\overset{↔}{CF}.$ Hence, 

$$
m∠BFC=m∠FBE={139}^{∘}.
$$

Now, using the angle addition postulate, we can find $∠AFB:$

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠AFB & =m∠BFC-m∠AFC \\  & ={139}^{∘}-{71}^{∘} \\  & ={68}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3

Given that AB↔∥CF↔, what is the measure of ∠AFB?

a
65∘
b
75∘
c
66∘
d
68∘
e
71∘
Submit
Correct

Notice that ∠BAF and ∠AFC are alternate interior angles formed when the transversal AF↔ cuts the parallel lines AB↔ and CF↔. Hence, m∠AFC=m∠BAF=71∘.

Also, notice that ∠FBE and ∠BFC are alternate interior angles formed when the transversal BF↔ cuts the parallel lines AB↔ and CF↔. Hence, m∠BFC=m∠FBE=139∘.

Now, using the angle addition postulate, we can find ∠AFB: m∠AFB=m∠BFC−m∠AFC=139∘−71∘=68∘
